recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Role: Host of the Innerverse Podcast, biofield tuning practitioner & researcher

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Cymatics and the Ordering Principle", "body": "The Gnostic Chef raised Cymatics as a plain answer for skeptics of sound healing, and Chance said he knew the premise without having researched it himself. He described vibration shaping sand on a plate, and argued that light, sound, scent and physical vibration were all the same energy at different points on the perceptual spectrum. Chance contrasted the entropy story of a cold heat death with what he called centropy, an ordering principle in the cosmos. He said coherent patterns pulled chaotic material toward order, and he presented himself as one coherent voice trying to spread that order."}, {"title": "Worldview Healing Before Frequency Fixes", "body": "Chance told the Gnostic Chef that he saw less value than many people did in Rife style machines, which he compared to treating symptoms rather than root causes. He said targeted frequencies might help break up malignant structures, but that a distortion would return if the psyche level issue behind it went unaddressed. He described using a weighted tuning fork on his own long-standing injury and finding that a related psychological issue resolved as well. Chance concluded that worldview healing and self-view healing were the only kinds that existed, and the host compared this to diets that fail without a mental shift."}, {"title": "Biofield Anatomy Beyond the Seven Chakras", "body": "Chance explained biofield tuning as using tuning forks to locate stuck emotions or limiting beliefs in the electromagnetic field around the body, with distance from the body indicating how old a person was when the experience formed. He said he was self taught after reading Eileen Day McKusick's Tuning the Human Biofield. He described the system as an expansion of the chakras, giving each of the seven centers four quadrants, for a mystical 28. When the host asked whether each center had its own consciousness, Chance answered that in a healthy person the centers flowed into one another like waterfalls between pools."}, {"title": "Fragmented Selves and Inner Parts", "body": "Chance proposed that a frozen fragment of life force could behave like a separate entity inside a person. He said many reported experiences of possession or attachment might be better described as a person's own self in conflict with itself. He added that he had met fully formed ego states in his practice, and that in his view they could not be fully dissolved, only coaxed into working together. He pointed to Internal Family Systems therapy, which he described as a guided way of letting self parts talk to one another, and said he hoped to cover it in future InnerVerse episodes."}, {"title": "Symbolic Literacy and Choosing Meaning", "body": "Chance argued that symbolic literacy mattered because, without a catalog of symbols and meanings, life looked like random events, while with it synchronicity appeared everywhere. He described the green language as a way of breaking words apart to find layered meanings. Chance told listeners to treat how much fun they were having as the best measure of well-being, and to say no to anything that was not a full body yes. He also said people were the source of meaning and could choose interpretations of their stories that felt expansive, while the host noted that taking responsibility could be hard."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: I sat down with The Gnostic Chef, host of Gnostic Chats, to talk about frequency healing, biofield tuning, and how symbols and beliefs shape our well-being.
